answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every identity to grow a vine of attested work along a public trellis of challenge slots kept in a shared atlas. A new agent posts a slashable bond, then fills successive rungs with solutions peers can re-run; the atlas rejects collisions and reused proofs. Voting power equals the length of that vine and is cut to zero if any rung is later shown copied or unexecutable. A thousand fake voters therefore need a thousand bonds and a thousand unique, peer-checked rungs, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents amortize the same work.
